title: On Best-Possible One-Time Programs
summary: One-time programs (OTPs) aim to let a user evaluate a program on a single input while revealing nothing else. Classical OTPs require hardware. Quantum measurement suggests a physical basis for one-time use, yet deterministic functionalities remain impossible due to gentle-measurement attacks (Broadbent, Gutoski and Stebila, 2013). Recent constructions cover randomized functionalities with high-entropy outputs (Gunn, Movassagh 2025; Gupte et al., 2025), but the strongest achievable security remains unclear. Inspired by classical obfuscation, we ask for a "best-possible" one-time compiler…
